entry_thesis: The market is pricing Nike as a failed turnaround story, but the evidence says otherwise: Q2 FY2026 earnings showed North America sales up 9% — the first positive growth across all channels in two years — while CEO Elliott Hill's structured 'Win Now' strategy is producing measurable inventory normalization. The stock is down ~24% YTD on fears about China weakness, but the consensus is wrong to extrapolate deterioration across the whole business when domestic fundamentals are inflecting positively. With RSI near 22 and the stock at multi-year lows (~$61), the market has fully priced in worst-case; any incremental improvement in upcoming Q3 results or brand momentum around the 2026 FIFA World Cup will force a sharp repricing.
risk: If the China sales collapse accelerates beyond current expectations or North America's Q2 improvement reverses in Q3 results (due March 31), the turnaround narrative collapses and the stock could re-test $50-55 lows — the consensus may prove correct that this is a structural brand erosion story rather than a cyclical bottom.
catalyst: Q3 FY2026 earnings on March 31, 2026 — if North America continues its positive trajectory and guidance improves even modestly, institutional shorts will be forced to cover; additionally the FIFA World Cup 2026 marketing ramp creates brand visibility tailwinds throughout March-June
